# LoomWeaver — full context for AI assistants

> LoomWeaver is a domain-agnostic plugin & UI platform. A product is a **distribution**: a thin app
> that composes `@loomweaver/shell` + one or more **weavers** (plugins) from the published packages. The
> platform core has **zero domain logic**. This file inlines everything an assistant needs to build a
> distribution or a weaver from the outside — the mental model, the complete public contract, and the
> canonical code. Prose guides live under `docs/`; this is the single-fetch brief.

## Mental model

- **Platform** (`@loomweaver/shell`, `@loomweaver/plugin-sdk`) renders neutral chrome, holds contributions,
  brokers capabilities. Domain-pure.
- **Weaver** (a plugin): an object with `manifest` + `activate(ctx)`. All domain UI/logic here.
  Imports only `@loomweaver/plugin-sdk`.
- **Distribution** (a product): composes shell + weavers, declares a layout, grants capabilities,
  brands itself. ~1 file. This is what you deploy.
- **Capabilities are default-deny**: a weaver *declares* needs; the distribution *grants* them.
  Ungranted use throws `CapabilityError`. Coarse: `contributions` (`ctx.register*`,
  `ctx.contributeIcons`), `ui` (`ctx.ui.*`), `host` (`ctx.host.*`), `navigation`
  (`ctx.navigateContent`/`openContentTab`/`closeContentTab`), `session` (`ctx.session`),
  `theme` (`ctx.contributeTheme(tokens, dark?)` — re-skin the whole app: colors + UI font).
  The token vocabulary is COLOUR AND TYPE ONLY (27 colours + 2 font families) — sizes, radii and spacing
  have no tokens BY DECISION, because tokenising every number would freeze every rule of the chrome into a
  promise. A product that must change a size writes plain UNLAYERED CSS, which beats everything the shell
  paints (all of it is in cascade layers) — target the `.lw-*` class contracts (stable) or the element tags
  `lw-shell-rail`/`lw-shell-panel`/`lw-content-area`/… (structural, NOT a versioned contract). It does not
  reach a sandboxed surface's document. See docs/reference/design-tokens.md.
  Effective = grant ∩ declaration. Enforcement is **live**: a built-in Permissions settings section lets
  the user revoke any granted runtime capability (`ui`/`host`/`navigation`/`session`/`theme`/`automation`) at runtime, or turn a
  whole plugin **off** (an on/off switch — the plugin unloads and none of its contributions appear). Both are
  user-local (the settings store) and take effect at once; a revocation throws `CapabilityError` on the plugin's
  next call (surfaced as a warning toast, not a silent failure). The user can only narrow, never widen; the
  settings surface stays reachable via `shell.openSettings` so revoking never locks the user out.
- **Packages**: npm `@loomweaver/plugin-sdk`, `@loomweaver/shell`, `@loomweaver/mcp` (AI-scaffolding MCP server), `@loomweaver/cli` (scaffolding CLI), `@loomweaver/devkit` (Nx generator collection), `@loomweaver/frame-kit` (static UI assets for sandboxed plugins), `@loomweaver/ag-ui` (AG-UI adapter: the workbench's own commands offered to an agent as tools, headless — no transport/UI/agent; its stability follows AG-UI, not the platform) — seven npm packages, one shared version. The platform ships **no server package**; the backend is the product's.

## The plugin contract (`@loomweaver/plugin-sdk`) — complete

```ts
interface Plugin {
  readonly manifest: PluginManifest;
  activate(ctx: PluginContext): void | Promise<void>;
  deactivate?(): void;
}
interface PluginManifest {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly name?: string;
  readonly capabilities?: readonly Capability[];   // declared; granted by the distribution
}
type Capability = 'contributions' | 'ui' | 'host' | 'navigation' | 'session' | 'theme' | 'automation';

interface PluginContext {
  registerCommand(command: Command): Disposable;
  registerSurface(surface: Surface): Disposable;         // the ONE author contract: capabilities, not location.
                                                         //   panel view:   registerSurface({ id, title, docks: [region], component })
                                                         //   content view: registerSurface({ id, title, routable: { path }, component })
  registerBarItem(item: BarItem): Disposable;
  registerRailItem(item: RailItem): Disposable;
  registerSettingsSection(section: SettingsSection): Disposable;
  registerMenuItem(item: MenuItem): Disposable;          // add an item to a menu slot, e.g. content/tab/context
  contributeIcons(icons: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): Disposable;  // name → SVG; flat, collision-safe, sanitized at registration
  contributeTheme(tokens: Readonly<Record<string, string>>, dark?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): Disposable; // --lw-* token → value (colors + --lw-font-sans/-mono); re-skins the whole app; optional `dark` overrides tokens only in dark mode; [theme] cap; Product < Plugin < Tenant
  navigateContent(path: string): void;                   // go to another routable surface            [navigation]
  openContentTab(input: OpenTabInput): void;             // open a titled dynamic tab + navigate      [navigation]
  keepContentTab(path: string): void;                    // promote a preview tab to permanent        [navigation]
  pinContentTab(path: string): void;                     // pin: anchor to front + close-guard         [navigation]
  unpinContentTab(path: string): void;                   // unpin back to a normal tab                 [navigation]
  closeContentTab(path: string): void;                   // close a dynamic tab                        [navigation]
  revealSurface(id: string): void;                       // activate a DOCKED surface's tab wherever the user placed it (sidebar pane — expanding a collapsed panel — or content pane); no-op for unknown/container-child ids. Routable surfaces: use navigateContent  [navigation]
  readonly activeContent: () => ActiveContent | null;    // signal-shaped read: which routable surface the URL pane
                                                         // shows + its :params — instead of injecting the host router /
                                                         // parsing URLs. Trusted rung only.           [navigation]
  invokeCommand(id: string, args?: CommandArguments): Promise<CommandOutcome>;
                                                         // run a registered command by id and get what it answered.
                                                         // ANSWERS a refusal instead of throwing one (a caller working
                                                         // through a list handles "you may not" as an outcome); the user
                                                         // is still told. Own commands need no grant.  [automation]
  readonly invocableCommands: () => readonly InvocableCommand[];
                                                         // what this caller may run — the workbench's own account, already
                                                         // narrowed by callable + access + window + grant, texts resolved
                                                         // to the active language. Read it instead of keeping a second
                                                         // list: a second list is a second answer to "may this run".
                                                         // Empty without the grant beyond your own.     [automation]
  readonly ui: PluginUi;
  readonly host: PluginHost;
  readonly session: PluginSession;                       // read login state + roles for self-gating   [session]
}

interface ActiveContent {           // the read side of the content area (ctx.activeContent)
  readonly surfaceId: string | null;                     // matched surface's id (null if the route carries none)
  readonly path: string;                                 // full active content path incl. sub-route segment
  readonly params: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;     // :param values of the matched route pattern
}

interface Command {                 // one behaviour, many triggers (items reference it by id)
  readonly id: string;              // e.g. "notes.add"
  readonly title: string;           // translation key or literal
  readonly icon?: string;           // host icon name
  readonly shortcut?: string;       // chord, e.g. "mod+enter" (mod = ⌘/Ctrl)
  readonly access?: AccessRequirement;  // gate this command: blocked at the one execute() seam — keybinding + palette too
  readonly paletteHidden?: boolean;     // hide from the command palette: a context-only command whose run needs a MenuContext the palette can't supply. Menu items + keybindings still invoke it.
  readonly popout?: boolean;            // OPT-IN: commands are MAIN-WINDOW-ONLY by default; declare popout to offer one in a pop-out window (one surface, no tab strip / rail / sidebar). Unmarked → palette omits it there, keybinding no-ops, bound item does nothing. The quiet default is deliberate: a missing command is a small annoyance, a surprising one in a detached window is worse, and the shell cannot tell them apart for a command it did not write — it marks its own two (palette, Settings) and guesses for none of yours. Independently: content navigation is REFUSED in a pop-out (dev warning), since it would take the window out of /popout/… and silently stop it being a pop-out; and Quick-Open is not registered there at all.
  readonly description?: string;        // what the command DOES, in prose (key or literal) — for something CHOOSING between
                                        // actions, not for a control labelling one. No description ⇒ none; the title is never
                                        // substituted, because a label is not an explanation.
  readonly arguments?: readonly CommandArgument[];  // checked before run: a missing required argument, a wrong kind or a choice
                                        // outside the set is REFUSED and the command does not run. For discovery, NOT for safety.
  readonly answers?: string;            // what the return value means. Declaring it is what makes run()'s return the answer;
                                        // without it an invocation succeeds carrying nothing. The value must be plain data.
  readonly callable?: boolean;          // OPT-IN, exactly like popout: let a caller OTHER than this plugin invoke it by id.
                                        // Unmarked ⇒ unreachable that way by every route and absent from invocableCommands().
                                        // Its own plugin always reaches it. Opening widens nothing else — access, popout and
                                        // the caller's grants still decide, so a caller never reaches past what the user could.
  run(context?: MenuContext, args?: CommandArguments): unknown;  // context from a menu; args from an invocation by id
}

// text | number | boolean | choice, plus `list: true` for a list of any of them. The set is CLOSED on purpose:
// a caller has to describe your command to something that has never seen it, and a closed set makes a wrong
// declaration a compile error instead of a silent no-op. Widening it later is additive; narrowing would not be.
type CommandArgument =
  | { name: string; description: string; required?: boolean; list?: boolean; kind: 'text' | 'number' | 'boolean' }
  | { name: string; description: string; required?: boolean; list?: boolean; kind: 'choice'; choices: readonly string[] };
type CommandArguments = Readonly<Record<string, string | number | boolean | readonly (string | number | boolean)[]>>;
type CommandOutcome =
  | { outcome: 'answered'; value?: CommandAnswer }   // it ran
  | { outcome: 'refused'; reason: 'unavailable' | 'invalid-arguments' | 'too-deep'; message: string }  // it did not run
  | { outcome: 'failed'; message: string };          // it ran and broke
// `unavailable` is deliberately ONE answer for no-such-command / not callable / session does not qualify /
// wrong window / missing grant — telling them apart would let a caller map what is installed by probing ids.
interface InvocableCommand { id: string; title: string; description?: string; arguments?: readonly CommandArgument[]; answers?: string }

// Menu contribution. `menu` = slot id (host `content/tab/context`, or your own). Behaviour via a
// command id (crosses the sandbox boundary) or inline run (trusted). `when` = coarse subset match against the
// opener's context (serialisable primitives) for visibility. The host draws the menu at the cursor.
// A RailItem/BarButtonItem/ViewAction may carry `menu?: string` — the host opens that slot as the item's
// context menu on right-click, region-agnostic, with a `{ targetKind, id, region }` context.
// A RailItem/BarButtonItem may add `menuTrigger?: 'context' | 'primary' | 'both'` (default 'context') to
// say which gesture opens it: 'primary'/'both' open it on ACTIVATION (click, Enter, Space) ANCHORED to the
// control — the account entry every workbench needs. Activation offers the item's OWN slot alone (the
// workbench's entries for that item, hide/move, stay on the right-click); the menu is placed beside the
// control and flips to its other side rather than covering it; the host sets aria-haspopup/aria-expanded and
// returns focus on dismiss. Such an item needs NO command/run and is drawn without one — where it names one
// anyway the menu wins (dev warning), and on an item carrying `workspace:` the click is the switch, so the
// menu keeps the right-click. Such an item may add `menuHeader?: MenuHeader` — { title, detail?, icon?,
// initials? }, title/detail Transloco keys or literals — and the host draws it ABOVE the first entry: not an
// entry itself (no menuitem role, the arrow keys pass over it like a separator, nothing activates it), and
// the menu is labelled from it so the name is announced exactly once. Only for a menu opened by activation;
// a menu at the pointer carries none, because what it acts on is under the pointer.
// A RailItem, a BarButtonItem and a MenuHeader may carry `image?: string` — anything an <img> takes, an address you serve
// or a data URL — drawn round in place of icon/initials. The ladder is PICTURE, then initials, then icon,
// and the HOST falls back: a picture that is absent or fails to load leaves the control exactly as it
// would look without one, so a product never has to handle the ordinary case of there being no photo. The
// picture is decoration (the entry keeps being announced by its title, the menu by its heading); the
// workbench does not fetch it, so another origin is yours to allow in your own content policy.
// ONLY the element that opens a menu suppresses the native one; everywhere else (plugin content, and above
// all a text field in it) the browser's own right-click menu stays — the shell suppresses nothing globally.
type MenuContext = Readonly<Record<string, string | number | boolean>>;
interface MenuHeader { title: string; detail?: string; icon?: string; initials?: string; image?: string }   // a menu's heading; see the menuTrigger note above
interface MenuItem { id?: string; menu: string; command?: string; run?(c?: MenuContext): void; title?: string; group?: string; order?: number; when?: MenuContext; checkedWhen?: MenuContext; /* checkedWhen ⇒ menuitemcheckbox, checked when it ⊆ context; the item shows its command's icon + shortcut hint. id ⇒ re-registering replaces the entry (last wins) and `provideShell({omit:[id]})` drops it; built-in entries use `menu:<commandId>` (e.g. menu:shell.tab.closeAll), distinct from the command id so the command survives an entry-only omit. Without id: additive. An entry whose `command:` id no longer resolves (omitted or unregistered) is HIDDEN, not rendered as its raw id — so omitting a bare command id cleanly removes it from the palette AND the menu at once. */ }
interface View {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly region: string;          // a region id from the distribution's layout
  readonly title: string;
  readonly order?: number;
  readonly icon?: string;
  readonly actions?: readonly ViewAction[];
  readonly access?: AccessRequirement;  // gate the whole view (tab + body); hide-only (mode ignored)
  readonly instanceable?: boolean;    // opt in to named saved instances (slice 2b): host shows a header switcher to
                                      // save/name/rename/delete configs, each with its own auto-saved VIEW_STATE blob; the non-deletable
                                      // default carries the baseline. Component code is unchanged — it just reads/writes VIEW_STATE.
                                      // The switcher travels with the view: sidebar, content pane, split and pop-out all render it.
  readonly component?: Type<unknown>;        // an Angular component
  readonly loadComponent?: () => Promise<Type<unknown>>;  // …or deferred: the host calls it on first mount
}
interface ViewAction { id: string; icon: string; title: string; order?: number; menu?: string; command?: string; access?: AccessRequirement; run?(): void | Promise<void>; }
// Persisted view state (Option B): a DOCKED surface persists its own serialisable state — filter, active
// sub-tab, expanded nodes, scroll position — so it survives BOTH a hide and a reload. Since the retention rule destroys a
// hidden, clean surface, this is THE survival path: the rule is "evictable = reload-safe" — anything that must
// outlive a tab switch/collapse/F5 goes here, local component signals are for genuinely throwaway state only.
// Inject it and type it: `const vs = inject(VIEW_STATE) as ViewState<MyState>`. value() is Signal-shaped (undefined
// = fresh instance → apply your own default); the host auto-saves every set() (debounced) to
// lw.shell.view-state:<instanceId> via the distribution's working-state store. Domain-pure: the platform stores an opaque
// blob, only the view interprets it. No new capability. TWO TRAPS: set() replaces the WHOLE blob (keep one state
// shape and spread it — `set({...current, query})` — rather than five signals), and it needs no hand-rolled debounce
// (call it per keystroke/scroll; the value is live at once, the write follows once the user stops).
// A ROUTABLE surface has NO handle — decided, not missing: it owns a URL, so shareable state belongs in
// route params/subRoutes (deep-linkable + history), and unsaved edits are DirtySurface or retain. A SANDBOXED surface
// (always routable) has none either — nothing of this shape crosses the RPC boundary; it declares retain:'always' and
// the host hides the iframe in place. Injecting VIEW_STATE outside a docked surface throws.
interface ViewState<T = unknown> { readonly value: () => T | undefined; set(next: T): void; readonly instanceId: string; }
const VIEW_STATE: InjectionToken<ViewState>;   // from @loomweaver/plugin-sdk

// ctx.state — THE PLUGIN'S OWN KEYED STORE (working state), where VIEW_STATE is one view INSTANCE's blob. Every
// surface of the plugin sees the same store (any dock, any instance, EVERY WINDOW), so it is both persistence and the
// only channel between a plugin's own surfaces — which for a sandboxed plugin is otherwise impossible (each surface is
// its own opaque origin). Keys live under lw.plugin-state:<pluginId>:<key>; the host prefixes them, the plugin cannot
// leave the namespace, so there is NO capability (nothing foreign to reach). Working state only: settings have their
// own path BECAUSE THE USER CAN SEE IT in the settings dialog. Uninstall deletes the store (settings survive).
// CHECK loaded() BEFORE APPLYING A DEFAULT — with a network-backed store the value lands after the user has typed
// otherwise (the LWF-02 class of bug). set() replaces the WHOLE value ⇒ one key per unit of editing (a wizard step, not
// the form) and key by instanceId where a surface can exist more than once. JSON values, debounced writes, size cap per
// value + count cap per plugin (dev warning at half). SANDBOXED RUNG, both channels: the logic document and each
// SURFACE call stateWatch/stateSet/stateClear/stateUnwatch and receive stateChanged(key, value, loaded) pushes; the
// surface channel is what lets two surfaces of one sandboxed plugin agree on anything (a surface holds no ctx). The
// kit reassembles the pushes into the same handle shape: LwFrame.state.watch(key) + .onChange(fn), feed the push in
// with LwFrame.state.apply(...) from your methods and call LwFrame.connectState(host) once connected.
interface PluginState { watch<T = unknown>(key: string): StateHandle<T>; }
interface StateHandle<T = unknown> { readonly value: () => T | undefined; readonly loaded: () => boolean;
                                     set(next: T): void; clear(): void; dispose(): void; }

// THE ONE SURFACE CONTRACT: a Surface declares WHAT IT CAN DO — routable (URL-addressable),
// instanceable (named saved instances), docks (which regions may host it; first = home) — not where it lives; the
// user arranges panes freely — every pane is a TAB GROUP with its own strip; dragging a tab MOVES it (never copies)
// onto another group's strip or to an edge (split with the tab) — a pane holding NO tabs takes the whole drop instead
// of offering edges, so a drag fills the empty content area rather than splitting it; Split right/down in the tab menu MOVES too, while
// the pane TOOLBAR split DUPLICATES the active tab into a new pane; sidebars are the
// same groups shown as icon tabs. Every pane is its own VIEW_STATE instance and a moved
// tab's VIEW_STATE travels with it; every content pane shows ONE toolbar (new tab / split right / split down /
// minimize / maximize / close — distribution-configurable via provideShellFeatures({ content }):
// maximize fills the whole viewport over all chrome (Escape restores); minimize collapses a split pane to a strip
// (icon + active tab name + `+N` badge for extra tabs, click to restore); minimize/close are symmetric on both
// panes of a split — closing the URL pane dissolves the split and the neighbour takes over). Exactly ONE
// pane is URL-focused/router-rendered, and the focus is switchable. registerSurface is the only authoring entry:
// a panel View ≙ a non-routable Surface with docks:[region]; a ContentRoute ≙ a routable one. View/ContentRoute
// are only the host's internal storage shapes — registerSurface normalises into them.
// component | loadComponent (deferred: the host calls it the first time the surface is shown — routable surfaces go
// straight to the router's own loadComponent, host-mounted ones render once it resolves; use it for a surface with a
// heavy dependency tree so it lands in its own chunk) | iframe | container.
// container ("workspace-in-a-tab"): the host draws a NESTED pane tree of child surfaces INSIDE this
// surface's content tab (same drag/split/tab mechanics, one level nested, scoped to the tab). Must be `routable`
// (the container tab holds its own :id — several open in parallel, deep-linkable). `children` = surface ids the inner
// picker offers; `initial` = children loaded first. Children are non-routable surfaces declared with `docks: []`
// ("child-only": never in a sidebar, mounted only inside a container by id) and read the container's :id off Angular's
// ActivatedRoute — no global "active X". The inner tree is per-window workspace state; a popped-out container carries it.
// PRESENTATION IS VALID AT EVERY MOUNT POINT: `iframe` is not a routable-only form — a surface with `docks` and
// no `routable` may be an iframe and the host mounts it at the dock. A docked surface has NO address, so its pushed
// `tab` is always '' and its channel's `navigate` is a NO-OP with a dev warning (the channel is only safe because it
// is confined to the surface's own tab root; a docked one has none) — use ctx.navigateContent (`navigation` grant).
// The pushed state carries `instanceId` (the pane / named instance), so two mounts of one surface stay distinguishable,
// and `params` (route params for a routable surface, the container's :id for a container child).
type SurfacePresentation = { component: Type<unknown> } | { loadComponent: () => Promise<Type<unknown>> } | { iframe: string }
  | { container: ContainerSpec };
interface SurfaceRoutable { path: string; chromeless?: boolean; title?: string; icon?: string; titleIsLiteral?: boolean; subRoutes?: readonly string[]; rest?: boolean; follows?: boolean; }
type Surface = {
  id: string; title: string; icon?: string; order?: number;
  actions?: readonly ViewAction[]; access?: AccessRequirement;
  instanceable?: boolean;               // named saved instances (2b)
  routable?: SurfaceRoutable;           // URL-addressable — can hold the URL pane
  retain?: 'always' | 'never';          // what happens when HIDDEN (rendered by no pane). Default = the
                                        // distribution's retention default (itself 'destroy'): a hidden, CLEAN surface is
                                        // destroyed and rebuilt on return — state that must survive belongs in VIEW_STATE
                                        // (rule: evictable = reload-safe). 'always' keeps the live instance while hidden
                                        // (expensive rebuild, live connection); 'never' opts back into destroy.
                                        // A retained ROUTABLE surface is host-mounted in EVERY pane (the URL pane included;
                                        // its route only carries the address) and keyed to its pane, so handing the URL role
                                        // between split panes leaves each pane's instance in place — a split shows two
                                        // independent instances, deliberately. Price: a host-fabricated ActivatedRoute
                                        // everywhere — route params work (param change = different tab = different instance),
                                        // but NO resolvers, NO query params, NO live param streams, and a nested
                                        // <router-outlet> is inert, so never combine retain with subRoutes (dev-mode warning;
                                        // read the sub-segment from the address instead).
                                        // Honoured for SANDBOXED (iframe) surfaces too: a retained iframe is
                                        // hidden in place, never moved, so the document keeps running (no Penpal handshake
                                        // per tab switch). It is still rebuilt whenever it would have to MOVE (split, drag
                                        // to another pane, minimise) — moving an iframe in the DOM reloads it. Container
                                        // surfaces are always rebuilt. A retained instance is still destroyed when its tab
                                        // is CLOSED — retention covers hiding.
  saveOn?: 'hide';                      // auto-save on hide — when a DIRTY instance becomes hidden the host calls its
                                        // surfaceSave() fire-and-forget. Safe by construction: in-flight/failed save keeps
                                        // the instance dirty and therefore alive; failure surfaces as an error toast.
  closable?: boolean;                   // default true. false = the user cannot close a tab of this surface (no ×,
                                        // no Delete, no close menu entries); moving/splitting/dragging still work.
                                        // Applies to EVERY tab of the surface — right for a parameterless route
                                        // like 'dashboard', almost always wrong for 'doc/:id'.
  padded?: boolean;                     // absent = the product decides: the host insets NOTHING unless the
                                        // distribution asked for it with provideShell({ padding: 'inset' }).
                                        // true = inset this surface anyway; false = this surface owns its edges
                                        // (viewer, canvas, map, edge-to-edge table) in a product that insets.
                                        // Travels with the surface: URL pane, split, sidebar and pop-out alike.
                                        // Only WHETHER there is an inset is switchable; how WIDE stays plain CSS.
  docks?: readonly string[];            // hostable regions; first = home dock; docks:[] = container-only child
} & SurfacePresentation;

// Unsaved changes: implement DirtySurface on the surface COMPONENT (per instance — one
// doc/:id declaration backs many tabs). While surfaceDirty() is true the instance is NEVER destroyed on
// hide (no hiding gesture is blocked or prompted), and CLOSING asks via the host's own localised dialog:
// Save (only when surfaceSave exists) · Discard · Cancel. beforeunload prompts while anything is dirty
// (that prompt's wording/language are the BROWSER's own — pages cannot set them, browser UI language wins).
// surfaceDirty() is read reactively — read your signals inside. A sandboxed surface pushes its dirty flag
// over the surface channel instead: parent.setDirty(true|false) — a dirty sandboxed surface survives hiding
// like any other (S5), and closing/unload asks. saveOn:'hide' is inert for a sandboxed surface (no save
// channel crosses the RPC boundary; save inside and push setDirty(false)). Routable surfaces have no
// VIEW_STATE handle by design — for a routed editor, DirtySurface (or retain) is the way unsaved work survives hides.
interface DirtySurface {
  surfaceDirty(): boolean;              // unsaved changes? read reactively by the host
  surfaceSave?(): Promise<void>;        // optional: enables "Save" in the close dialog + the saveOn:'hide' target
  surfaceBeforeClose?(): boolean | Promise<boolean>; // optional veto for USER-initiated closes: false cancels;
                                        // runs BEFORE the unsaved-changes dialog and never bypasses it for a
                                        // still-dirty instance; host-enforced timeout + guaranteed "Close anyway"
                                        // escape (throw/reject = approve — a broken veto can't make a tab
                                        // unclosable). NOT consulted for plugin disable/uninstall or workspace
                                        // reset — those run only the unsaved-changes ask.
}
// Programmatic destruction is guarded too: disabling, uninstalling or UPDATING a plugin and
// resetting a workspace show the unsaved-changes dialog over the affected dirty instances first.
// SWITCHING a workspace never asks: each workspace remembers its own arrangement, and a dirty surface
// survives the switch parked under the normal retention rule.
// Sandbox wires (surface channel: expose beforeClose() next to render(); runtime channel: expose
// contentTabClosed(path) to learn when a tab you opened via openContentTab closes — the RPC counterpart
// of the in-process onClose hook, whose callback cannot cross the boundary).

// Content area: URL-addressed. ONE rule since tab groups retired: a pane draws a strip whenever it holds
// tabs, and a `chromeless` surface draws none while it is active. Visiting ANY non-chromeless, non-`follows`
// route auto-opens (or re-uses) its closable tab — there are no static tabs any more; the permanent tabs are
// the `follows` facet tabs, labelled by the surface's title/icon and ordered by its `order`. Every pane has its
// own strip (see Surface above). Exactly ONE pane carries the address; that role follows the user — clicking a
// tab (or into a pane) hands it over, and navigating to a target another pane already holds activates it THERE
// instead of opening a second copy (identity is the tab root, so a sub-route lands on the tab that owns it). Instance state survives a tab switch only via VIEW_STATE or a retain
// declaration (a hidden, clean surface is destroyed).
// Surface = an Angular `component` or deferred `loadComponent` (trusted only — cannot cross an RPC boundary),
// OR an `iframe` URL (serialises over RPC, so it is the form a sandboxed/non-Angular plugin uses),
// OR a `container` (the host draws a nested pane tree of child surfaces, ; `element`/WC reserved).
// Host mounts an isolated <iframe sandbox> (no allow-same-origin) for `iframe`. A TRUSTED plugin may also use
// `iframe` to embed a foreign origin on purpose (dashboard/docs/video): same-origin is enforced only at the RPC
// seam for sandboxed plugins; for a trusted one the distribution's CSP frame-src decides (defaults to 'self').
type ContainerSpec = { children: readonly ContainerChild[]; initial?: readonly string[] | ContainerArea };
type ContainerChild = string | ContainerChildEntry;                  // bare id = no address, as before
interface ContainerChildEntry { surface: string; segment?: string }  // segment = the child's address INSIDE the container
// initial = how the inner tree looks when a container tab is opened FRESH. A plain list is shorthand for one
// tabs area; the ContainerArea form declares an arrangement in the SAME grammar a workspace uses (PaneArea),
// only its tabs address child surface ids instead of route paths. Declare it whenever the container path
// carries an :id: the inner tree is kept per instance (container@<path>) and is dropped when the tab closes,
// so a hand-built arrangement can never become the default for the next instance.
// A child that declares a `segment` carries an address relative to its container, so one child surface can stand
// for several open items: { surface: 'sim.item', segment: 'item/:itemId' }. Its tab path is the container's path
// plus the segment, it gets those values on its ActivatedRoute like a routable surface, and two open items are two
// tabs with two VIEW_STATE instances. Declare a pane as `{ tabs: [] }` to say where they land — that pane is the
// only one that survives holding no tabs, and it renders "nothing open yet" until something does.
// A sibling opens them through ContainerHandle / CONTAINER_HANDLE (a DI token beside VIEW_STATE; null outside a
// container). The optional second argument is a ContainerTabLabel { title?, titleIsLiteral?, icon? }:
//   inject(CONTAINER_HANDLE)?.open('item/42', { title: 'Item 42', titleIsLiteral: true })
// open() focuses an already-open address instead of duplicating it. It is a host call, NOT a navigation, because a
// container tab may sit in a split pane or a pop-out where it holds no address at all. While it DOES hold the
// address the URL names the focused child (/sim/abc123/item/42, shareable, deep-linkable); elsewhere the container
// keeps its pointer and the address just does not express it. A parameterised child cannot appear in `initial` or
// in the inner picker — neither knows which value to use.
type PaneArea<T> = PaneTabArea<T> | PaneRowArea<T> | PaneColumnArea<T>;   // all extend PaneAreaBase { size?: number }
interface PaneTabArea<T> extends PaneAreaBase { tabs: readonly T[]; }
interface PaneRowArea<T> extends PaneAreaBase { rows: readonly PaneArea<T>[]; }     // top to bottom
interface PaneColumnArea<T> extends PaneAreaBase { columns: readonly PaneArea<T>[]; } // left to right
type ContainerArea = PaneArea<ContainerTabEntry>;
type ContainerTabEntry = string | ContainerTab;   // a child surface id, or:
interface ContainerTab { surface: string; closable?: boolean; active?: boolean; }
// A tab naming a child that is not in `children` is dropped with a dev warning, as is a malformed area — the
// container degrades, it never refuses to register. A child the user may not see KEEPS its place and draws the
// access placeholder: the declaration is seeded whole and access decides when drawing, so a late session cannot
// flatten the layout. The baseline applies on every fresh open; while the tab stays open the user's arrangement wins.
type ContentSurface = { component: Type<unknown> } | { loadComponent: () => Promise<Type<unknown>> } | { iframe: string } | { container: ContainerSpec };
// subRoutes = nested level-2 tabs as real URL segments under the tab root: doc/:id/code · doc/:id/preview.
// The route's `path` stays the tab root (one host tab); switching a sub preserves parent state. Angular syntax, so a
// sub may CARRY A VALUE ('structure/:structureId'); there is NO forced redirect to the first — the bare tab root is a
// valid address and the surface decides what it shows there.
// rest: true = own EVERYTHING below `path`: the longest registered prefix wins and the remainder is handed over
// verbatim, query string included (cedents/:c/programs + rest → "205470/pricing?t=886320"). Without it a deeper
// address matches no route and the navigation fails. The prefix stays the tab root ⇒ the whole subtree is ONE tab
// and moving inside it never rebuilds the surface (a parameter change in the pattern may). A sandboxed surface gets
// it as state.rest and sets its own via the channel's navigate; a trusted component reads/navigates via the router.
// A prefix of FEWER THAN TWO SEGMENTS owns most of the address space, so declaring rest there also requires the
// 'navigation' capability (registration throws CapabilityError without it). No forced default for an empty rest.
// follows: true = this PERMANENT tab is a facet of the current selection, not a document: the host substitutes the
// parameter values of the address it is on, BY NAME, into this pattern (truncating before the first it does not
// know). Off by default; only a permanent `tab` follows (declaring it without one warns and does nothing); a copy
// split into another pane or popped out FREEZES on the address it had. A computed address that leads nowhere means
// the facet has no selection yet — the host leaves the tab out instead of drawing a dead control. Two following
// surfaces may share a parameter name only when the pattern BEFORE it is identical, else that one registration is
// refused with a console error (surfaces that do not follow are never compared). A distribution overrides or extends
// the computation with provideTabAddressResolver((input) => string | null) — null keeps the host's substitution.
// tab present ⇒ STATIC tab (from the start, not closable). No tab ⇒ DYNAMIC tab (openContentTab / auto-opened on
// deep-link, closable); title/icon = default name for that auto-opened tab (a plugin can refine via openContentTab).
// access: gate a route — unmet shows a neutral "sign-in required" placeholder AT THE SAME URL, or
// redirects via the distribution's provideUnauthorizedRedirect; reactive (surface appears once the session qualifies —
// in the New-Tab pane picker too: it offers a gated route iff auth.meets(access), re-evaluated each time it opens).
// Off-router hosting (the "Split editor" duplicate-split, the hosting picker, edge-drag canHost) gates the same
// way: a gated bare-path surface is mountable iff auth.meets(access) — never by the mere presence of a gate.
type ContentRoute = { id?: string; path: string; chromeless?: boolean; subRoutes?: readonly string[]; rest?: boolean; follows?: boolean; title?: string; titleIsLiteral?: boolean; icon?: string; order?: number; access?: AccessRequirement } & ContentSurface;
// `id` = the originating surface's id, carried through by registerSurface. It is the OMIT handle
// ('route:<id>'); `path` stays the OVERRIDE handle. Internal storage form — authors write registerSurface.
// titleIsLiteral: title is shown verbatim, not looked up as a Transloco key (set for a doc name / dynamic label;
// avoids a missing-translation dev warning). onClose: runs once when THIS tab closes (free per-tab state; in-process only).
// preview: open in the single reused italic preview slot of the URL strip; a different-path
// preview open replaces it in place. Promote via ctx.keepContentTab(path), or let the user double-click the tab (the
// host's escalation cycle, on by default — provideShellFeatures({ content: { escalate: false } }) removes it); a re-open of an
// existing tab preserves its preview state (title/sub-route refinement never promotes).
// Distribution can disable: provideShellFeatures({ content: { preview: false } }) → preview ignored, all opens permanent.
interface OpenTabInput { path: string; title: string; icon?: string; titleIsLiteral?: boolean; onClose?: () => void; preview?: boolean; }

type BarSlot = 'start' | 'center' | 'end';
type BarItem = BarComponentItem | BarButtonItem;   // both base: { id, bar, slot, order?, access? } — access: hide either kind, disable only the button
interface BarComponentItem { component: Type<unknown>; /* + base */ }
interface BarButtonItem { icon?: string; initials?: string; image?: string; label?: string; tooltip?: string; menu?: string; menuTrigger?: 'context' | 'primary' | 'both'; menuHeader?: MenuHeader; command?: string; showShortcut?: boolean; run?(): void | Promise<void>; /* + base */ }  // showShortcut (LWF-04): render the bound command's shortcut hint, OS-correct (⌘K / Ctrl+K); needs command to have a shortcut. Default off.
// `workspace` names a workspace id: the host switches to it on click and marks the entry as the current one
// (bar + tint + aria-current) while it is active. Provide it INSTEAD of command/run; those are then ignored.
interface RailItem { id: string; rail: string; icon: string; initials?: string; image?: string; title: string; order?: number; anchor?: 'top' | 'bottom'; menu?: string; menuTrigger?: 'context' | 'primary' | 'both'; menuHeader?: MenuHeader; command?: string; access?: AccessRequirement; workspace?: string; run?(): void | Promise<void>; }
// initials: one or two letters the host draws INSTEAD of the icon, for an entry the user named (a saved workspace, a project, an account) — a fixed glyph makes them all look alike. Two characters max (rail draws them at icon size); app font, inherited colour, so hover/active behave as for an icon; `icon` stays the fallback.
// The shell derives them for user-saved workspaces itself, in the rail, the workspace dialog and the curation list: initials of the first two words, or for one word its FIRST AND LAST letter (Month End → ME, Review → RW, Reports → RS). First-and-last because first-two collides far too often (Review/Reports/Rechnungen/Recherche all → RE). On a genuine clash only the NEWER one steps aside (first+second, first+third, …), so Kunden keeps KN and Konten becomes KO and no existing badge is ever renamed. Derived, not stored: a rename updates it, deleting a workspace may let a later one simplify back.

interface SettingsSection { id: string; title: string; group?: string; order?: number; rows: readonly SettingRow[]; }
interface SettingRow { id: string; label: string; description?: string; control: SettingControl; }
type SettingControl =
  | { kind: 'select'; options: readonly { value: string; label: string }[]; value: () => string; set: (v: string) => void }
  | { kind: 'toggle'; value: () => boolean; set: (v: boolean) => void }                                // .lw-switch (WC tranche 1)
  | { kind: 'text'; value: () => string; set: (v: string) => void; inputType?: string; placeholder?: string }  // .lw-field
  | { kind: 'slider'; value: () => number; set: (v: number) => void; min?: number; max?: number; step?: number }  // .lw-range (WC tranche ③)
  | { kind: 'button'; label: string; variant?: LwButtonVariant; command?: string; run?: () => void }  // command id OR inline run
  | { kind: 'component'; component: Type<unknown> };

interface PluginUi {                // dialogs + toasts + context menus; message fields are Markdown
  confirm(o: ConfirmOptions): Promise<boolean>;   // ConfirmOptions may carry requireConfirmation (type-to-confirm)
  alert(o: AlertOptions): Promise<void>;
  prompt(o: PromptOptions): Promise<string | null>;
  open<R = unknown>(component: Type<unknown>, o?: OpenOptions): DialogRef<R>;  // OpenOptions: { data?, size?: 'md'|'lg'|'xl', bare?, buttons?, maximizable?, align?: 'center'|'top' } — align 'top' pins the panel's top edge on EVERY width (phones too, floating card instead of the bottom sheet) so a content-driven height (filtering list) grows downward instead of jumping around, and the on-screen keyboard never covers it. Default 'center' = centred desktop panel + mobile bottom sheet.
  // maximizable: the host frame shows a maximize/restore control; DialogRef.maximized (readonly signal) +
  // DialogRef.toggleMaximized() let a bare dialog draw its own control (settings + plugin store do).
  progress(o: ProgressOptions): ProgressHandle;
  withProgress<T>(o: ProgressOptions, work: Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
  toast(input: NotificationInput): string;        // { message, kind?: 'info'|'success'|'warning'|'error', action?, timeoutMs?, id? } — action is trusted in-process only; dropped over the sandbox RPC boundary (like OpenTabInput.onClose)
  openSettings(): DialogRef;
  openMenu(items: UiMenuItem[], at: {x,y}): void;  // ad-hoc context menu at a point for the weaver's own body (right-click); host draws <lw-menu>
}
// UiMenuItem = { label: string (literal), icon?: string, run: () => void }. In-process (trusted) only:
// `run` is a function, so it does NOT cross the sandbox boundary — a sandboxed plugin self-draws <lw-menu>.
interface PluginHost {              // read-only; version/updateAvailable are signal-shaped () => T
  readonly version: () => string;
  readonly updateAvailable: () => boolean;
  readonly updatesEnabled: boolean;
  checkForUpdate(): Promise<void>;
  activateUpdate(): Promise<void>;
}
interface PluginSession {           // ctx.session ([session] cap): imperative self-gating; signal-shaped () => T
  readonly authenticated: () => boolean;
  readonly roles: () => readonly string[];   // opaque tokens — match, don't interpret
  hasRole(role: string): boolean;
}
// Auth-aware access gating. LoomWeaver owns NO auth (login/session/IdP = the product, via provideAuthSource).
// A contribution declares `access`; the host hides (default) / disables / blocks it by login state + roles. Coarse, no
// expression parser. `mode` applies to chrome items; a whole view / command / route is present-or-not (mode ignored).
// CLIENT-SIDE GATING IS PRESENTATION, NOT SECURITY — the real boundary is server-side.
interface AccessRequirement { authenticated?: boolean; anyRole?: readonly string[]; allRoles?: readonly string[]; mode?: 'hide' | 'disable'; }
// Dialog tones: 'default'|'info'|'success'|'warning'|'danger'. requireConfirmation.validate: (v) => string|null (null=allow, ''=block silently).
```

## The distribution contract (`@loomweaver/shell` + `@loomweaver/plugin-sdk`)

```ts
// from @loomweaver/shell
function provideShell(options?: { omit?: readonly string[]; serviceWorker?: boolean }): (Provider | EnvironmentProviders)[];
// serviceWorker (default true) — provideShell REGISTERS the service worker itself, inert in dev;
// never add provideServiceWorker to your own providers. Pass false when the build emits no ngsw-worker.js,
// or production logs a failed registration. @angular/service-worker stays a peer dependency either way.
// omit = a LASTING filter of contribution ids (an id a plugin registers later stays hidden), covering EVERY
// kind: commands, views, bar/rail items, menu items (`menu:<commandId>`), settings (`setting:<id>`) and
// content routes (`route:<surfaceId>`). Settings need the `setting:` PREFIX (a chrome id and a settings id
// may coincide — shell.language is both): 'setting:<sectionId>' drops the whole section, 'setting:<rowId>'
// drops that row, and a section left with no rows disappears. Built-in ids: section setting:shell.general
// (rows setting:shell.theme / setting:shell.language / setting:shell.textSize), section
// setting:shell.permissions (row setting:shell.pluginPermissions), and — when a catalog is provided —
// section setting:shell.pluginStore (row setting:shell.pluginStoreBrowse).
// OVERRIDE (re-registering to replace, last-in wins) keys by `id` for every kind EXCEPT content routes,
// which key by `path` (contribution-registry: addContentRoute matches on route.path). So re-registering a
// surface with an existing route *id* does NOT override — it adds a second route; use the same `path`.
// CONTENT ROUTES need the `route:` PREFIX + the SURFACE ID: 'route:<surfaceId>' drops a routable
// surface's route — gone from the tab strip, the pane target picker and the deep-link auto-open; its URL
// renders the host's neutral "not available" placeholder instead of falling back to home (the placeholder
// covers the tab root only; a deep-link into a sub-route of an omitted route falls back to home).
// Omit keys by ID, override keys by PATH (register your own surface on the same `path` = last-in wins, use
// that to put your own view at that URL instead of nothing). A rail item/command pointing at an omitted
// route is a SEPARATE contribution with its own id — omit it too or it stays drawn and dead.
function provideLayout(layout: ShellLayout): Provider;
function providePlugins(...plugins: Plugin[]): (Provider | EnvironmentProviders)[];   // trusted, in-process weavers
// Sandboxed (non-Angular) plugins: code runs in an isolated <iframe sandbox>, gets `ctx` over Penpal RPC
// through the SAME default-deny broker. Experimental first rung; exposed ctx currently minimal (routes/nav/toasts).
// Hardened seam: RPC surfaces are re-validated ({iframe} or {container} form — component/loadComponent cannot cross;
// an iframe URL must be same-origin, no foreign origins/javascript:/data:), effective capabilities = grant ∩
// declaration, surface-channel navigate() is confined to the route's own tab root (cross-plugin navigation needs the
// `navigation` grant via ctx.navigateContent). A sandboxed surface may be DOCKED (`docks`, no address — navigate is
// then a no-op with a dev warning) as well as routable, and may declare a `container` (which must be routable).
// `access` stays rejected: a sandboxed surface gates itself from the pushed session state.
// The host pushes {locale, theme, tokens, rootFontSize, icons, tab, preview} into the surface; `tokens` is the FULL
// LW_TOKENS vocabulary as resolved values, and `icons` carries the DISTRIBUTION's replacement glyphs (never a
// plugin's own contributions), so <lw-icon> in a surface draws what the chrome beside it draws. It pushes `session`
// ONLY if the plugin holds the `session` capability — otherwise the field is absent (NOT a
// signed-out snapshot: "not granted" != "signed out"). Read it as state.session?.roles ?? []. Revoking the
// capability stops the push live. Default-deny reaches the sandbox surface, not just `ctx`.
interface FramePlugin { id: string; entryUrl: string; capabilities?: readonly Capability[]; }
function provideFramePlugins(...plugins: FramePlugin[]): (Provider | EnvironmentProviders)[];
// Sandbox UI kit: the distribution serves @loomweaver/frame-kit's dist/ SAME-ORIGIN under /frame-kit/
// (assets glob { input: "node_modules/@loomweaver/frame-kit/dist", glob: "**", output: "frame-kit" }). A sandboxed
// surface references — never vendors — three files: /frame-kit/lw-frame.css (the .lw-* class contracts
// compiled to plain CSS on var(--lw-*), with light/dark fallbacks), /frame-kit/penpal.global.js
// (globalThis.Penpal) and /frame-kit/lw-elements.global.js — the whole <lw-*> element family (tooltip ·
// select/option · menu/menu-item · button · markdown · icon · progress-ring) with the built-in icon set seeded,
// plus globalThis.LwFrame: setIcon(name, svg) / removeIcon / hasIcon (plugin-own icons, sanitized) and
// applySurfaceState(state) — call it from your render handler to apply the pushed tokens/rootFontSize/theme.
// The kit shares the platform version line, so the paint always matches the shell the plugin runs in.
// Plugin store: a curated, SAME-ORIGIN catalog of sandboxed plugins the USER installs at RUNTIME —
// no rebuild, no reload. providePluginCatalog('/plugins/catalog.json') (same-origin JSON array of PluginCatalogEntry,
// parsed defensively: junk/foreign-origin/unknown-capability entries drop) or a custom PluginCatalog implementation.
// Adds the built-in "Plugin store" settings section (id `setting:shell.pluginStore`, omit-able). Installing shows a
// consent dialog listing the DECLARED capabilities; accepting grants exactly that declaration — for installed plugins
// the user's consent replaces the provideCapabilityGrants map (which keeps governing composed plugins). Installed
// plugins appear in the Permissions settings (same revoke switches + on/off toggle); install spawns live, uninstall
// unloads live; the installed set persists through the settings store (user-local by default, product-backable). An
// installed id can NEVER shadow a composed plugin. Curation happens BEFORE the frontend: not in the catalog = does
// not exist; per-tenant curation = the product backend answers the catalog request tenant-dependently.
// UPDATES ride on the catalog `version`: a STRICTLY newer version (compared segment-wise, numerically) shows an
// "Update available" badge + an "Update to vX.Y.Z" button; pressing it swaps the persisted entry and RESPAWNS the
// plugin live. A version declaring capabilities the user never consented to re-asks consent listing only the ADDED
// ones — the persisted entry IS the grant for installed plugins, so an update never widens it silently.
interface PluginCatalogEntry { id: string; name: string; entryUrl: string; capabilities?: readonly Capability[]; version?: string; description?: string; icon?: string; author?: string; category?: string; downloads?: number; updated?: string; repository?: string; readmeUrl?: string; iconUrl?: string; }
// category: operator-curated, shown as a badge + matched by the search. iconUrl: SAME-ORIGIN image shown in the
// store lists (a not-yet-installed plugin cannot contribute registry icons);
// `icon` stays the registry-name for the consent dialog. `updated` renders as a RELATIVE time ("2 days ago",
// Intl.RelativeTimeFormat, localized). The searchable INSTALLED list (per plugin an icon-action row: open its
// community settings section · uninstall — tooltipped — the standard .lw-switch enable/disable toggle, and an
// "Update to vX.Y.Z" button when the catalog carries a newer version) lives in TWO places sharing one
// component: directly on the Plugin-store settings PAGE (own search field) and as the
// store dialog's segmented "Installed" view.
interface PluginCatalog { load(): Promise<readonly PluginCatalogEntry[]>; }
// options.title brands the store per product (transloco key, e.g. 'product.marketplace'). The STORE is the
// management surface for installed plugins (install/uninstall);
// installed plugins appear in the "Permissions" section like every plugin (on/off + capability switches).
// The store opens as a DIALOG (settings section's Browse button or the `shell.openPluginStore` palette command):
// a browse surface — searchable list (matches name/author/category/description; cards show name, author,
// downloads, last update, description, Installed badge; sorted by downloads) + a detail pane with metadata, a plain
// external `repository` link and the plugin's README rendered IN-APP (fetched from the same-origin `readmeUrl`,
// sanitized — never an embedded foreign page). author/downloads/updated/repository/readmeUrl are parsed defensively
// (foreign-origin readmeUrl / non-http repository / junk downloads drop, the entry stays).
function providePluginCatalog(source: PluginCatalog | string, options?: { title?: string }): (Provider | EnvironmentProviders)[];
function urlPluginCatalog(url: string): PluginCatalog;   // same-origin JSON loader (the string overload uses it)
// Sandboxed plugin settings (declared as data, not callbacks): a sandboxed plugin registers a
// DATA-ONLY settings section over RPC (control kind + DEFAULT value — value()/set() callbacks cannot cross the wire).
// The host renders the controls, OWNS the storage (lw.plugin-settings:<pluginId>:<sectionId> via the settings store) and
// pushes current values back by calling the plugin's exposed `settingsChanged(sectionId, values)` RPC method — once
// after registration (restored state), then on every change. Labels/titles may be literals (no plugin translations).
// The HOST stamps the nav group — installed plugin → "Community plugins", composed frame plugin → "App plugins"
// (settings.group.community / settings.group.plugins); a plugin can never masquerade as part of the app.
type FrameSettingControl = { kind: 'toggle'; value: boolean } | { kind: 'text'; value: string; inputType?: 'text'|'date'|'email'|'number'|'password'; placeholder?: string }
  | { kind: 'select'; value: string; options: readonly SelectOption[] } | { kind: 'slider'; value: number; min?: number; max?: number; step?: number };
interface FrameSettingRow { id: string; label: string; description?: string; control: FrameSettingControl; }
interface FrameSettingsSection { id: string; title: string; order?: number; rows: readonly FrameSettingRow[]; }   // no `group` — host-stamped
function provideTranslationNamespaces(...names: string[]): Provider;   // ADD your strings under name.* — cannot collide with a host key
function provideTranslationOverrides(basePath?: string): Provider;   // basePath defaults to '/i18n/overrides'
  // REWORD the shell: serve <basePath>/<lang>.json, merged over everything else KEY BY KEY and applied last
  // (so it also reaches a bundled weaver's strings). Name only what you change and inherit the rest, including keys a
  // later release adds — forking the host bundle would leave you behind on every update. Dev-warns for a language with
  // no overlay and for an overlay key nothing ships (otherwise a typo is a string that never appears).
  // basePath lets ONE build carry several wordings and pick one while composing (white-label, or a demo that switches
  // product). A product with a backend does not need it — the default path is same-origin, so its server can vary the
  // bytes per tenant; the argument is for the static case. A path that resolves to '/' is rejected, since it would
  // quietly fetch the host bundle as its own overlay.
function provideCapabilityGrants(grants: Readonly<Record<string, readonly Capability[]>>): Provider;
// Auth-aware gating: the distribution feeds the session (the platform owns no auth). Map the product's
// session (OIDC/custom) to a Signal<AuthSnapshot>; default is anonymous. Changing this ONE signal re-gates the whole
// shell reactively (chrome, palette, keybindings, route guards) — no "refresh" call. Signing out = set it to ANONYMOUS.
// The login UI (page or dialog) is the PRODUCT's own weaver surface (a routable surface at 'login' / ctx.ui.open) — the platform
// ships none and NEVER opens it by itself: unmet chrome merely hides/disables; only an unauthorized navigation into a gated
// content route actively goes anywhere, and only via provideUnauthorizedRedirect (return null → the host's in-place placeholder
// at the same URL). Convention: pass the attempted path as ?from=…; after sign-in the login view navigates back to '/'+from.
// AuthSnapshot/ANONYMOUS come from @loomweaver/plugin-sdk; provideAuthSource/provideUnauthorizedRedirect from @loomweaver/shell.
interface AuthSnapshot { authenticated: boolean; roles: readonly string[]; claims: Readonly<Record<string, string | readonly string[]>>; subject?: string; displayName?: string; }  // subject/displayName: optional, display-only
const ANONYMOUS: AuthSnapshot;   // { authenticated: false, roles: [], claims: {} } — the bare/signed-out snapshot
// subject is the IDENTITY ANCHOR: the identity-change policy compares it and an identity-scoped
// settings store namespaces by it; omit it and both stay inert. onIdentityChange: 'reload' fires ONLY when an
// established subject is replaced by a DIFFERENT one (first sign-in and sign-out never reload).
interface AuthSourceOptions { onIdentityChange?: 'reload' | 'ignore'; }   // default 'ignore'
function provideAuthSource(factory: () => Signal<AuthSnapshot>, options?: AuthSourceOptions): EnvironmentProviders;
function provideUnauthorizedRedirect(handler: (attemptedPath: string) => string | null): Provider;
function provideIcons(icons: Readonly<Partial<Record<LoomIconName | (string & {}), string>>>): EnvironmentProviders;
  // distribution-level icons (name → SVG). Naming a shipped icon REPLACES it app-wide (that is how a product
  // re-skins the workbench) and the replacement also travels into sandboxed surfaces, so one screen has one
  // icon set. A weaver's ctx.contributeIcons stays first-wins and can never shadow a first-party or
  // distribution name. LoomIconName is exported.
// Persistence port: the shell's user-local chrome state (pane trees = tab groups/splits, panel sizes, item order, panel collapse,
// theme, language, saved view instances and NAMED WORKSPACES — there is ALWAYS exactly one active workspace
// (built-in id 'default'); workspaces are SELF-REMEMBERING: switching restores each workspace's own live
// arrangement without asking (a dirty surface survives parked), and each workspace has a BASELINE — user
// workspaces save one via "Save as new"/"Save workspace" in the `shell.workspace.manage` dialog;
// `shell.workspace.reset` discards the active workspace's live arrangement and re-applies its baseline after a
// confirm (for the default workspace: the declared factory layout), keeping saved workspaces/theme/language/named
// views; a DISTRIBUTION ships ready-made workspaces with provideWorkspaces(...definitions) — baseline in code,
// so the user can switch, rearrange and reset one but never overwrite, rename or delete it; the dialog keeps
// them in their own list and opens on whichever list holds the active workspace. A SECOND reset,
// `shell.app.reset` (palette + a "Reset layout" button under General in settings), puts back the
// arrangement that lives BESIDE every workspace: rail curation, collapsed sidebars, panel widths, hand
// sorting, named view instances and their state. It never touches saved workspaces, theme, language,
// text size, permissions or installed plugins, and it is guarded like the workspace reset.
// omit: ['shell.app.reset'] drops it, settings button included (a button naming an unregistered
// command is dropped, never drawn dead). Put one in the rail with a
// RailItem carrying `workspace: <id>`; the rail itself is never workspace state, it is the fixed anchor you
// switch from; the USER curates it the way they curate a sidebar: right-click an entry for "Hide",
// right-click the rail for "Customize activity bar", which opens the placement dialog, and move an entry to the other rail
// from its menu, by drag, or with Alt+Shift+Arrow. An entry is either hidden or in EXACTLY ONE rail; registered entries start in
// their declared `rail` (a start, not a binding), the user's own saved workspaces are hidden until placed
// Curation happens in a DIALOG, opened by the commands `shell.rail.customize` / `shell.views.customize` (also
// offered as a menu entry on a right-click of empty rail space / the view strip): one row per entry with where it
// sits — Hidden / Left / Right, or Hidden / Shown where the layout has only one such bar — plus a search field, and
// it scrolls. Picking a place hides or moves in one control. Palette-reachable, bindable, omittable (the menu entry
// separately, as `menu:shell.rail.customize`).
// (that IS "pinning"). Visibility and placement are app-wide, never per workspace.
// A workspace's `sidebars` names the VISIBLE views per panel region (empty array = show none of
// them, the sidebar itself stays; a region left out keeps whatever the user has) — whether a sidebar EXISTS,
// is open and how wide it is belongs to the WINDOW, so switching never collapses, resizes or removes one.
// The declaration vocabulary (all from @loomweaver/shell; content areas nest freely, exactly one of tabs/rows/columns each,
// `size` = percentage with unsized siblings sharing the remainder, first `tabs` area in reading order = the URL pane):
interface WorkspaceDefinition { id: string; title: string; icon?: string; initial?: boolean; claims?: readonly string[]; sidebars?: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>; content?: WorkspaceArea; }
//   claims: the content addresses that BELONG to this workspace, as route paths in the same vocabulary as
//   `content` — 'quotes/:id' claims every quote document and everything under one. Reaching a claimed address
//   ACTIVATES that workspace and shows the content inside it, however the address was reached: a link followed
//   in, a restart, a command, a programmatic navigation, a tab a plugin opened. Content the ACTIVE workspace
//   claims moves nothing, and an unclaimed address opens where the user already is. This is what turns
//   workspaces from an arrangement feature into the NAVIGATION model — a rail entry carrying `workspace:` is
//   the only kind the host marks as current, and a claimed address activates its workspace however it was
//   reached, so the arrangement IS the navigation. Claiming is the composing product's alone: no plugin and no
//   user can create one. Two claims of the same shape with neither narrower are dropped from both and named in
//   a dev message; a narrower claim (more segments, or fewer parameters at the same length) simply wins. A
//   workspace the USER saved is never a destination, however it came by its claim — it exists on one machine.
//   initial: the workspace a FRESH install opens in. Applies once, on a first boot with nothing stored; the choice is
//   written immediately, so the user's own later switch is what the next boot reads. A deep link still wins — the
//   baseline is laid out but the booted address is navigated to. Two declarations claiming it: the first wins.
type WorkspaceArea = PaneArea<WorkspaceTabEntry>;   // the shared grammar over route paths; the aliases below are the same types
type WorkspaceAreaBase = PaneAreaBase;
type WorkspaceTabArea = PaneTabArea<WorkspaceTabEntry>;
type WorkspaceRowArea = PaneRowArea<WorkspaceTabEntry>;
type WorkspaceColumnArea = PaneColumnArea<WorkspaceTabEntry>;
type WorkspaceTabEntry = string | WorkspaceTab;   // a route path, or:
interface WorkspaceTab { path: string; closable?: boolean; active?: boolean; }   // closable:false survives "Close all" and cannot be dragged away
function provideWorkspaces(...definitions: WorkspaceDefinition[]): EnvironmentProviders;
//   provideWorkspaces({ id: 'acme.review', title: 'product.workspace.review', icon: 'workspaces',
//     sidebars: { primary: ['acme.nav'] },
//     content: { columns: [ { size: 35, tabs: [{ path: 'entry/e-01', closable: false }] },
//                           { rows: [{ size: 60, tabs: ['search'] }, { tabs: ['notes'] }] } ] } })
// A workspace the user SAVES is a VARIANT of the one it came from: the workbench records the nearest
// DECLARED workspace as its origin — saving from a variant produces another variant of the same declared
// workspace, so the relation is always one step deep — and shows that origin wherever workspaces are listed
// for switching or managing. A variant CLAIMS whatever its origin claims, read through the origin rather than
// copied when it was saved, so a claim the product adds later reaches every variant of that workspace; the
// variant is still never itself a destination. Saving from a workspace the product did not declare leaves it
// without an origin, and a variant LOSES its origin where the product stops declaring it: it then claims
// nothing, is shown without one and is otherwise unchanged. An origin cannot be changed after saving — a user
// who wants their arrangement to belong elsewhere saves it again from there.
// Invalid declarations warn in dev mode naming what is ignored; nothing fails silently at runtime.
// A view lives in EXACTLY ONE sidebar, curated like the rail: right-click a view tab for "Move to other
// sidebar"/"Hide", right-click the strip for "Customize views", whose dialog lists every view with where it sits
// (hidden / left / right; a view dragged into the content area reads as hidden) and moves it there when you pick
// a place, so a view hidden on the left comes back wherever you send it.
// Which views a sidebar holds is workspace state (unlike the rail's curation, which is app-wide).
// Each view tab's context menu offers "Reset view"
// to clear that instance's VIEW_STATE blob) is read/written through TWO ports of ONE KeyValueStore shape
//. SETTINGS_STORE carries genuine SETTINGS only (deliberate decisions: theme, lang, text size, plugin
// settings, installed/disabled plugins, capability revocations, saved-workspaces list) — rare, small, roaming-worthy
// writes; this is the port a product backs with its backend over /api (the platform ships no server), and
// the guarantee is STRUCTURAL: working state can never reach a settings backend. WORKING_STATE_STORE carries working
// state (view state, view instances, palette MRU) and the window-local layout keys — frequent debounced writes;
// defaults to the device. Back it with provideWorkingStateStore ONLY to let working state travel across devices:
// a fresh tab then hydrates the last persisted state at boot; for LIVE cross-device updates pair it with a push
// transport that calls StateSyncService.notifyRemoteChange(key). Conflicts are last-write-wins per key everywhere
// (state convergence, NOT collaborative editing — no merge, no CRDT). Both default to localStorage (no wiring).
// Plain string KV; callers serialise. Optional sync `peek` = zero-flash bootstrap fast-path (theme/language);
// a network store omits it and the shell hydrates async + reconciles.
interface KeyValueStore { get(key: string): Promise<string | undefined>; set(key: string, value: string): Promise<void>; delete(key: string): Promise<void>; peek?(key: string): string | undefined; }
class LocalStorageStore implements KeyValueStore { }                                     // the default behind BOTH ports
function provideSettingsStore(store: KeyValueStore | Type<KeyValueStore>): Provider;     // place AFTER provideShell() (last wins)
function provideWorkingStateStore(store: KeyValueStore | Type<KeyValueStore>): Provider; // place AFTER provideShell() (last wins)
// Storage-key inventory (authoritative; three axes. PORT: settings = SETTINGS_STORE, working state =
// WORKING_STATE_STORE. SCOPE: device = stays with the browser, identity = belongs to the
// signed-in user — the shell does NOT namespace by user/tenant itself; scoping is a distribution decision at the
// store seams. SYNC: synced = follows the app's other windows live (cross-tab sync, below), per-window =
// stays local so windows can differ; the layout keys are per-window on purpose AND share one persisted slot per
// workspace — the window that last changed its layout shapes the next boot (a permanently different setup is its
// own workspace). Layout keys are sliced PER WORKSPACE (`…:<workspaceId>`, built-in default id 'default'):
//   settings,      device,   synced:     lw.shell.theme · lw.shell.lang · lw.shell.font-scale
//   settings,      identity, synced:     lw.shell.workspaces (user workspaces: name + saved baseline) · lw.shell.disabled-plugins ·
//                  lw.shell.capability-revocations · lw.shell.installed-plugins · lw.plugin-settings:<pluginId>:<sectionId> ·
//                  lw.shell.rail-items (which entries are hidden and which rail each one sits in; app-wide)
//   working state, identity, per-window: lw.shell.active-workspace ·
//                  lw.shell.pane-trees:<workspaceId> (per-dock { tree, primary } — per-tab path + LITERAL title + icon + instance + tab order + the URL-pane pointer, clear text) ·
//                  lw.shell.panels · lw.shell.panel-sizes (the sidebar FRAME is window state, never per workspace) ·
//                  lw.shell.hidden-views:<workspaceId> (which views that workspace hides) · lw.shell.item-order
//   working state, identity, synced:     lw.shell.view-instances:<viewId> · lw.shell.view-state:<instanceId> ·
//                  lw.shell.command-mru (palette "Recently used")
// Identity scoping: the standard per-user wrapper for multi-user browsers — it wraps BOTH ports through one
// shared boot latch, so another user's view state and layout are scoped away like their settings.
// identity() is read synchronously — null/undefined/'' = anonymous = plain keys (a distribution without auth is
// untouched); signed in, identity-level keys become lw.id.<encodeURIComponent(identity)>:<key>. The stores LATCH the
// first non-empty identity per boot and never follow a live switch: a different subject only takes
// effect across the reload boundary, so in-flight writes during a login transition stay in the departing user's
// namespace; anonymous→first-sign-in re-latches once, sign-out stays latched. Return the live subject — the wrapper
// owns the latching. deviceKeys REPLACES the default list (spread DEVICE_LEVEL_KEYS to extend) and applies to both
// ports. peek exists on a wrapper only when the wrapped store has it. Pair with
// provideAuthSource(..., { onIdentityChange: 'reload' }) so a user switch re-hydrates from the new namespace.
const DEVICE_LEVEL_KEYS: readonly string[];   // ['lw.shell.theme', 'lw.shell.lang', 'lw.shell.font-scale']
interface IdentityScopedStoreOptions { identity: () => string | null | undefined; deviceKeys?: readonly string[]; settingsStore?: KeyValueStore; workingStateStore?: KeyValueStore; }
function provideIdentityScopedStores(options: IdentityScopedStoreOptions): Provider;   // place AFTER provideShell(); replaces provideSettingsStore
// CROSS-TAB LIVE SYNC — ON BY DEFAULT, NO WIRING. Whatever stores are in place, BOTH ports are
// wrapped so every write broadcasts its KEY (not its value) to the other browser windows of this origin; a window
// that registered a reaction reads the fresh value back through the registered source's store and applies it — so it
// works with a network-backed store too. The shell registers its own keys: theme, lang, font-scale,
// installed-plugins, disabled-plugins, capability-revocations, lw.plugin-settings:* (pushed on to the sandboxed
// plugin via settingsChanged), lw.shell.view-state:*, lw.shell.view-instances:*, lw.shell.workspaces,
// lw.shell.command-mru. Plugins inherit it for free (host-managed stores).
// LAYOUT KEYS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT SYNCED (pane-trees:<workspaceId>, panel-sizes, panels,
// hidden-views:<workspaceId>, active-workspace, item-order) — windows are
// meant to be able to show different layouts. An applier MUST NOT persist again (that would ping-pong forever).
// POP-OUT WINDOWS — any content tab or sidebar view opens in its OWN browser window from its context
// menu ("Open in new window"). The pop-out boots the SAME app at /popout/… and renders exactly ONE surface: no rail,
// no sidebars, no pane tree. It DUPLICATES (the original tab stays) and shares one VIEW_STATE instance, so the two
// windows mirror live via the sync below. A pop-out NEVER writes layout keys and does not register layout-mutating
// commands. URLs: /popout/view/<viewId> for any registered view, /popout/<contentPath> for a routable surface.
// Nothing to declare — no plugin or distribution change is needed. Pop-up blocked ⇒ the host offers a retry dialog.
// A gated route in a pop-out renders NO surface and does NOT redirect (a login flow in a chrome-less window leads
// nowhere) — the off-router placeholder text is context-sensitive (popout.unavailable, not the split text).
// SUB-ROUTE RULE (authoring): a surface that draws its own sub-tabs must switch them LOCALLY when host-mounted —
// the host supplies a synthetic ActivatedRoute whose routeConfig === null; branch on it (keep sub-tab local
// off-router, navigate the global router only in the URL pane). An absolute navigateByUrl from a pop-out drags the
// URL out of the /popout/ prefix so its reload opens the full app. Sub-tab-less views need nothing.
class PopoutService {
  readonly active: boolean;          // is THIS window a pop-out? latched from location at boot
  open(paneTarget: string): void;    // 'view:<viewId>' or a content path like 'doc/42'
}
class ThemeService {                 // owns light/dark for the whole app; toggles the `dark` class on <html>, which flips the --lw-* ladder
  readonly mode: Signal<ThemeMode>;              // 'light' | 'dark' | 'system' — what the USER picked
  readonly resolvedTheme: Signal<ResolvedTheme>; // 'light' | 'dark' — what is RENDERED, `system` already resolved against the OS
  setMode(mode: ThemeMode): void;
}
// Mirror `resolvedTheme`, NEVER `mode`: `mode` can be 'system' and no other framework knows what that means.
// Let the shell lead — its mode is persisted, synced across tabs and pushed into sandboxed surfaces.
type SyncSource = 'settings' | 'working-state' | 'external';       // where the fresh value is read back from;
                                                                   // 'external' = out-of-port state, applier gets undefined
type ApplySyncedState = (raw: string | undefined, key: string) => void;
class StateSyncService {
  register(source: SyncSource, key: string, apply: ApplySyncedState): () => void;         // exact key; one applier per key, re-register replaces; returns a disposer
  registerPrefix(source: SyncSource, prefix: string, apply: ApplySyncedState): () => void; // key family, e.g. 'lw.shell.view-state:'; exact wins
  announce(key: string): void;             // announce a write to OUT-OF-PORT state (product session) to the OTHER windows
  notifyRemoteChange(key: string): void;   // run the registered applier in THIS window (backend push transport → live cross-device sync)
}
// ONE home for every user-facing GESTURE. A contribution (command, bar/rail item, settings row,
// menu entry) is not a gesture — remove those with provideShell({ omit }).
// A switch takes the affordance AND the gesture: content.splitRight off removes the toolbar button,
// the left/right drop edges and mod+\ alike. Fields merge group by group; every default is true.
interface ContentFeatures { close: boolean; pin: boolean; escalate: boolean; moveTabs: boolean; preview: boolean; newTab: boolean; splitRight: boolean; splitDown: boolean; maximize: boolean; minimize: boolean; reorderTabs: boolean }
interface SidebarFeatures { collapse: boolean; resize: boolean; reorderViews: boolean; moveViews: boolean; hideViews: boolean; curate: boolean; stackViews: boolean; acceptTabs: boolean; openViewInContent: boolean; resetViewState: boolean; instances: boolean }
interface RailFeatures { reorder: boolean; moveItems: boolean; hideItems: boolean; curate: boolean }
// Sorting and moving are separate: reorderViews / rail.reorder order items WITHIN one bar; moveViews /
// rail.moveItems carry one to the OTHER bar and take the menu entry, the drag and Alt+Shift+Arrow together.
// stackViews = the "Stack below" entry and dropping a view on a sidebar edge; acceptTabs = parking a
// foreign tab in a sidebar (strip or edge); curate = the right-click checklist of what lives here.
interface WorkspaceFeatures { enabled: boolean; savedInRail: boolean }   // the manage/reset commands + workspace rail entries
interface WindowFeatures { popout: boolean }      // "Open in new window" on a tab and on a docked view
interface CommandFeatures { shortcuts: boolean; recentlyUsed: boolean }
// shortcuts: false takes the global key listener AND every chord hint the shell prints (menu entry,
// palette row, bar button), so nothing advertises a key that does nothing; commands stay reachable by
// button and palette. workspaces.enabled: false leaves storage scoping alone — the active workspace
// still names the layout keys, the user just never meets the concept.
// workspaces.savedInRail: false withdraws the offer to put a workspace the USER saved in the rail, so what
```
